ideas.title: Add Regex ParamType for regular expression pattern matching validation
ideas.summary: Introduce a `Regex` parameter type (`click.Regex(pattern, flags=0, error_message=None)`). When converting a string value, it validates the string against the compiled regular expression. If the pattern does not match, it raises `BadParameter` with either the custom `error_message` or a default message displaying the value and pattern.
ideas.why_new: Click's `types.py` provides `Choice`, `IntRange`, `FloatRange`, `DateTime`, `Path`, and `File`, but lacks a general pattern-matching parameter type for validating arbitrary string formats such as UUIDs, semver strings, or custom codes.

ideas.title: Add SecretString ParamType with complexity and length constraints
ideas.summary: Add a `SecretString` parameter type (`click.SecretString(min_length=0, max_length=None, require_digits=False, require_uppercase=False, require_lowercase=False)`). It converts string input while enforcing minimum/maximum character length and character class rules. If validation fails, it raises `BadParameter` explicitly identifying which complexity requirement was not met.
ideas.why_new: Click currently has basic string types and `password_option` for masking input, but lacks a parameter type for validating complexity and length rules on secrets, passwords, or token options.

ideas.title: Add mutually_exclusive parameter group constraint rule to Command
ideas.summary: Add a `mutually_exclusive` argument to `Command.__init__` accepting a list of parameter name tuples (e.g. `[('foo', 'bar'), ('baz', 'qux')]`). During parsing and execution, if more than one parameter from any declared mutually exclusive group is explicitly supplied by the user (source is not default), Click raises a `UsageError` listing the conflicting options.
ideas.why_new: Click commands do not natively enforce mutually exclusive option groups at the command declaration level without writing custom parameter callbacks or using external plugins.

ideas.title: Add value_transform pipeline processing for Argument and Option parameters
ideas.summary: Extend `Parameter` (and inherited `Option`/`Argument` classes) with a `value_transform` parameter accepting a callable or list of callables. After standard type conversion and parameter callbacks succeed, each callable in `value_transform` is executed in order to normalize or sanitize the value (e.g. `str.strip`, `str.lower`) before passing the final value to context arguments.
ideas.why_new: Click parameters support type conversion (`type`) and a single `callback` for value resolution, but lack a post-conversion value transformation pipeline for chaining reusable normalization steps.

ideas.title: Add conditional option requirements via required_if and forbidden_if on Option
ideas.summary: Add `required_if` and `forbidden_if` parameters to `Option` constructor. `required_if` accepts a target option name or `(param_name, value)` tuple that makes this option required when the condition evaluates to true. `forbidden_if` prohibits this option if another specified option is present. If rules are violated during parse handling, Click raises `BadOptionUsage` detailing the constraint rule.
ideas.why_new: Options currently support unconditional `required=True`, but conditional requirements based on the presence or value of other CLI options must be hand-coded inside callbacks.

ideas.title: Add option_group decorator for grouping and attaching option sets
ideas.summary: Add an `option_group` decorator function (`click.option_group(name, *options, help=None)`) in `decorators.py`. It accepts a group name, help text, and a sequence of `@click.option` declarations, returning a single composite decorator that applies all contained options to the command function and attaches grouping metadata.
ideas.why_new: Click provides `@option`, `@argument`, `@group`, `@command`, but lacks a mechanism to bundle multiple option definitions into reusable named option groups across multiple command handlers.

ideas.title: Add error_handler decorator for mapping custom exceptions to CLI exit codes
ideas.summary: Add an `error_handler` decorator function (`click.error_handler(exception_type, exit_code=1, message=None)`) in `decorators.py`. When attached to a command callback, if the decorated function raises an instance of `exception_type`, Click catches it, formats and prints `message` (or str(e)) to stderr, and exits with `exit_code` instead of bubbling an unhandled traceback.
ideas.why_new: Command callbacks must manually catch domain exceptions or let them unhandled; Click lacks a declarative decorator to map internal exception classes directly to clean error messages and exit codes.

ideas.title: Add assert_exit_code and assert_output assertion helpers to CliRunner Result
ideas.summary: Extend `Result` in `click.testing` with explicit assertion methods: `Result.assert_exit_code(expected_code)` and `Result.assert_output(contains=None, matches=None, excludes=None)`. If an assertion fails, it raises an `AssertionError` with detailed diagnostic details combining exit codes, exception tracebacks, and captured standard streams.
ideas.why_new: `Result` objects hold standard test execution attributes (`exit_code`, `output`, `stdout`, `stderr`), but offer no built-in assertion helpers for clean testing assertions.

ideas.title: Add SectionedHelpFormatter with custom section priority and section headers
ideas.summary: Introduce `SectionedHelpFormatter` extending `HelpFormatter` with `section_priority` ordering support. Sections added during help generation are buffered by section priority rather than printed strictly in call order. When `getvalue()` is invoked, sections are formatted and rendered sorted by their declared priority level.
ideas.why_new: `HelpFormatter` streams text sequentially directly into an internal buffer as section methods are called, offering no priority-based section sorting or deferred section ordering.

ideas.title: Add SafeOutputFile context manager for atomic file writes with backup retention
ideas.summary: Add `SafeOutputFile` class and helper `open_safe_output_file(filename, mode='w', create_backup=False)` in `click.utils`. It writes output to a temporary file in the target directory and atomically renames it upon closing. If `create_backup=True`, any existing target file is moved to a `.bak` path before replacement. If an exception occurs during writing, the temporary file is removed and the original file is left unchanged.
ideas.why_new: `click.utils.open_file` supports basic lazy and atomic replacement, but lacks a dedicated context manager with automatic backup creation (`.bak`) and explicit rollback handling upon exceptions.

ideas.title: Add prompt_choices function for interactive multi-selection menus in termui
ideas.summary: Add `prompt_choices(text, choices, default=None, min_choices=1, max_choices=None, split_char=',')` to `termui.py`. It presents an indexed list of menu options, parses user input split by `split_char`, validates selected indexes/keys against `min_choices` and `max_choices` constraints, and returns a list of selected choice items.
ideas.why_new: Click's `termui` provides single-value `prompt()` and binary `confirm()`, but lacks a multi-selection prompt function for selecting multiple items from an options list.

ideas.title: Add CompletionFilter strategy engine for configurable completion matching
ideas.summary: Add a `CompletionFilter` class to `shell_completion.py` with `filter_completions(items, incomplete, match_mode='prefix')` supporting `'prefix'`, `'substring'`, and `'fuzzy'` strategies. Extend `ShellComplete` with a `match_mode` parameter that uses `CompletionFilter` to filter dynamic completion candidates before formatting output.
ideas.why_new: `ShellComplete` implementations use basic string prefix checks without an extensible strategy engine for substring or fuzzy completion candidate matching.

ideas.title: Add environment profile registration and selection to CliRunner
ideas.summary: Add `register_env_profile(name, env_dict)` method to `CliRunner` and a `profile` parameter to `CliRunner.invoke(..., profile=None)`. Pre-registered environment dictionary profiles (e.g. `'admin'`, `'readonly'`) can be activated by name during test invocations, merging profile variables with invocation-specific environment variables.
ideas.why_new: `CliRunner.invoke` accepts an `env` dictionary on each call, but `CliRunner` lacks named environment profile registration for reusing standardized environment contexts across multiple test runs.

ideas.title: Add retry attempt limits and custom failure messaging to prompt
ideas.summary: Extend `prompt()` in `src/click/termui.py` with `max_attempts` (default `None`) and `retry_message` parameters. When input fails type conversion or validation, `prompt()` retries up to `max_attempts` times printing `retry_message`. If `max_attempts` is exceeded, it raises `click.UsageError` or `click.Abort` indicating validation retry limits were exceeded.
ideas.why_new: `prompt()` currently loops indefinitely until valid input is received or EOF occurs, without options to cap validation attempt counts or customize retry error prompts.
